title: `st.cache_resource` and `st.cache_data` should support async functions (coroutines)
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

This was originally requested in #3651 for the deprecated `st.cache`, and the same problem still exists with  `st.cache_resource` and `st.cache_data`.

### `st.cache_data`
```python
import asyncio

import streamlit as st


[USER].cache_data
async def get_data():
    return 42


async def main():
    data = await get_data()
    st.write(data)


asyncio.run(main())
```
This results in the following error because the returned value of `get_data()`, a coroutine object, is not pickleable.
```
UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type get_data()) in get_data(). st.cache_data uses [pickle](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pickle.html) to serialize the function’s return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see [our docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/caching) for differences).
```

### `st.cache_resource`

```python
import asyncio

import streamlit as st


[USER].cache_resource
async def get_resource():
    return 42


async def main():
    resource = await get_resource()
    st.write(resource)


asyncio.run(main())
```

It runs successfully at the first run, but the following error occurs in the second run and later because the coroutine object returned from `get_resource()` is cached and the same coroutine object is awaited again.
```
RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine
```

### Why?

_No response_

### How?

I think it's enough the sample code snippets above work as expected.

### Additional Context

I'm an author of [stlite](https://github.com/whitphx/stlite) (Wasm ver. of Streamlit) and [Transformers.js.py](https://github.com/whitphx/transformers.js.py) (a Python wrapper for FWs like stlite to use Transformers),
and I encountered a situation where I wanted this feature: https://github.com/whitphx/transformers.js.py?tab=readme-ov-file#stlite-serverless-streamlit
The Transformers' object can only be obtained in an async way, and it's a compute-intensive task so I wanted to cache it. Now I do it using the session state as a workaround.

Hi, and thank you for opening / upvoting this issue
Sorry [USER], I forgot to answer to this issue (mostly because I didn't have an elegant answer). 

Stremalit cache primitives work with sync functions, you couldn't decorate an async function, but:
you can call an async operation inside a cached function in separate thread (to have isolated event loop):

This should work correctly, and the result should be very close to what you want:


```python
import asyncio
import streamlit as st
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor


[USER].cache_data
def get_data(x:int) -> int:
    # Use a separate thread to run the async operation
    # This lets us create an isolated event loop that won't conflict
    def run_in_thread(x:int) -> int:
        async def _async_operation(x:int) -> int:
            await asyncio.sleep(1)
            return x ** 2

        return asyncio.run(_async_operation(x))

    # Execute in a separate thread and wait for the result
    with ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
        return executor.submit(run_in_thread, x).result()


async def main():
    x = st.slider("Pick a number" , 0, 10)
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    data = get_data(x)  # Synchronous call
    st.write(data)


asyncio.run(main())

```

[USER] Also if your main streamlit app is not run by `asyncio.run(main())`, and it is just a python sync script, you can do a async call in your cached function in more laconic way:



```python
import asyncio

import streamlit as st


async def get_data(number):
    await asyncio.sleep(2)
    return number ** 2

[USER].cache_data
def get_cached_data(number: int):
    return asyncio.run(get_data(number))

x = st.slider("x", 0, 100)

st.write(get_cached_data(x))
```

I wrote a twisted function transformer in my library https://github.com/jokester/streamlit-concurrency to use `st.cache_data()` with async function. [demo in st cloud](https://concurrency.streamlit.app/cached_async)

Internally it uses `st.cache_data` to cache a sync function waiting for `asyncio.run(the_real_async_fun())` result in an executor thread. Similar to the pattern mentioned in other comments.

[USER] this will be included in the 1.64 release -- I just merged a PR so if you want to try this in the nightly then that is possible as well. 

Note, there were a lot of product decisions on what exactly to support here. The PR has a document exploring them linked, and I also made some issues for areas that are still unsupported (see mentions above). Please let me know if you have any feedback on these decisions, and whether further support is needed for your use cases!
